How to buy crypto safely in your country: exchanges and P2P

Buying is where many beginners lose money, usually to a fake site or a fake payment, not to the market. A few rules make the first purchase much safer.

Choose where to buy

  • A licensed or well-known exchange. It is simple, has rules and support, and usually asks for ID. Check on your regulator's website that it is allowed in your country.
  • P2P on an exchange platform. You buy from another person by bank transfer or mobile money, while the platform holds the crypto in escrow until payment is confirmed.
  • Never buy from strangers in chats or social media outside a platform with escrow. There is nobody to help you if something goes wrong.
  • Payment methods differ by country. Check which bank or mobile money options the platform supports before you deposit.
  • Local rules matter. In some countries banks restrict crypto payments, or crypto trading is limited. Check with your national regulator first.

Safe P2P, step by step

  1. Use the platform's own P2P market with escrow. Choose sellers with many completed trades and a high completion rate.
  2. Read the seller's payment terms. Pay only through the method and account shown in the order, never to a different account.
  3. Pay from an account in your own name. Payments from third parties are often rejected or reversed.
  4. Press “paid” only after you really paid. If you are the seller, release the crypto only when the money is in your own account. A screenshot is not proof.
  5. Keep every message inside the platform chat. If there is a dispute, use the platform's appeal process, not a private chat.

Common traps

  • Fake payment screenshots shown to you when you are the seller.
  • A seller or buyer who asks you to chat or pay outside the platform.
  • Bank transfers that are reversed later. Wait until the funds are final in your account.
  • Fake exchange websites and apps. Open the exchange from its official site or store page and read the address letter by letter.
  • A price far better than the market. Compare with a price page such as CoinGecko before you trust an offer.

Good habits

  • Start with a small amount to learn the process.
  • Turn on two-step verification for your exchange account before you deposit anything.
  • Keep records of your purchases. Tax rules differ by country, so check yours.
  • Never borrow money to buy crypto. Use only money you can afford to lose.

Tools mentioned in this guide

  • CoinGecko

    Prices, market caps and basic data for thousands of coins.

    How to start (5 steps)
    1. Open the CoinGecko website and type the token's name or ticker in the search box.
    2. Pick the result with the right name and symbol. Fake tokens copy names, so compare the contract address on the page with the one the project publishes on its own website.
    3. Look at market cap, 24-hour trading volume and the number of markets. Very low volume, or one tiny market, means a single trade can move the price.
    4. Use the official website and social links listed on the token page, not links sent to you in a chat.
    5. Open the price chart with the longest range to see the whole history, and check which exchanges list the token.

    CoinGecko shows data. It does not tell you whether a token is safe or will rise.

    Level: Beginner
